title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD & Roadmap (Q4 2026 - 2027)
author: Emma Chen
body:
Overview
========
Short intro:
Redwood's Unified Inference product bundles the Redwood API, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes with a set of developer-first controls for routing, cost-performance tuning, and rollout safety. This document summarizes the product vision, prioritized requirements (PRD), high-level design specs, roadmap themes (Q4 2026 - 2027), pricing & packaging guidance, and release notes for the current launch.

Goals and success metrics
-------------------------
- Goal: Make predictable, cost-effective LLM inference the default for engineering teams by offering a single API and a consistent operational model across hosted, dedicated, and private modes.
- Success metrics (target 12 months):
  - 99.95% API availability for hosted customers (SLA tier).
  - Average 95th-percentile latency <= 150ms for short chat requests in the Hosted Standard tier.
  - 20% reduction in per-token unit cost for customers migrating to recommended batching + caching defaults.
  - 30 enterprise accounts on Dedicated or Private contracts.

Product scope (what's in scope for this PRD)
-------------------------------------------
1) Unified API surface for: text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking, function/tool calling.
2) Smart routing: policy-driven routing (latency, cost, region, customer tier) + automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
3) Cost & performance controls: per-route batching, KV-prefix caching, quantization recommendation hints.
4) Rollouts: canary/A-B, automatic rollback, model pinning and versioning.
5) Observability: per-route token cost breakdown, latency histograms, and quality regressions tied to eval prompt sets.
6) Packaging + pricing: Pay-as-you-go hosted tiers, Reserved capacity (Dedicated) contracts, and Private licensing.

Out of scope (for this release)
--------------------------------
- First-party training and model hosting (only inference).
- Native on-device inference targets.

User personas and primary journeys
----------------------------------
- Persona: Backend engineer at an AI-native startup
  - Journey: sign up -> import prompts -> test locally -> select Hosted Standard -> enable caching -> observe reduced token costs -> promote to production.
- Persona: Platform engineer at enterprise
  - Journey: evaluate perf profiles -> request Dedicated PO -> configure autoscaling policy -> rollout across regions -> integrate RBAC and audit logging.

Requirements (PRD)
------------------
Priority is expressed as P0/P1/P2. Acceptance criteria are included.

Functional requirements
1. API parity (P0)
   - Description: Single REST/SDK surface supporting generation/chat/embeddings/reranking and streaming.
   - Acceptance criteria: Existing public SDKs can perform a generator and embedding request with equivalent parameters and receive expected response schemas.
2. Model routing (P0)
   - Description: Route requests based on latency budget, cost preference, region, and customer tier.
   - Acceptance criteria: Admin console shows routing rules; e2e tests validate fallback to next-best compatible model when capacity constrained.
3. Batching & caching controls (P0)
   - Description: Per-route settings: batch window (ms), max tokens per batch, enable prefix-KV caching with TTL.
   - Acceptance criteria: Config changes take effect within 5 minutes; enabled caching lowers token consumption on repeated prefixes in perf tests by >=15%.
4. Rollouts & canarying (P1)
   - Description: Canary rollout by percentage of traffic with automatic rollback on error/SLO violation.
   - Acceptance criteria: Canary can be configured for any route; rollback triggers within 60s when error rate > 2% or latency SLO breached.
5. Observability (P0)
   - Description: Per-route dashboards with token cost, latency (p50/p95/p99), error rates, and recent quality regression alerts.
   - Acceptance criteria: Dashboard displays data within 30s of ingestion and supports drill-down by model version and time range.

Non-functional requirements
- Reliability (P0): Platform SLO for hosted API of 99.95%; error budget policy documented.
- Performance (P0): 95th-percentile latency targets by workload class.
- Security (P0): Audit logging enabled for Dedicated/Private; keys via KMS/HSM for Private customers.
- Scalability (P0): Autoscaling rules for Dedicated pools with burst capacity cushion >=20%.

Design & architecture highlights
--------------------------------
- Runtime abstraction: Single request path with pluggable backends (hosted pool, dedicated pool, private endpoint).
- Kernel & perf selection: Model profiles (quantization/sequence length) used by runtime to select optimized kernels.
- Smart router: Policy engine evaluates request attributes and current capacity signals and assigns request to the lowest-cost compatible backend within the latency budget.
- Caching layer: Global prefix cache + per-customer KV cache with TTL and invalidation hooks.
- Observability pipeline: Traces and metrics exported via OTLP to Redwood Console; token-level cost computed in the ingestion pipeline and surfaced per-route.

Representative config table (example per-route settings)
-------------------------------------------------------
| setting_key | type | default | description |
| batch_window_ms | int | 20 | Max batching window to wait for additional requests |
| max_batch_tokens | int | 4096 | Maximum tokens in a batch to avoid long tail latency |
| caching_enabled | bool | true | Enable prefix KV caching for this route |
| cache_ttl_sec | int | 3600 | TTL for cached prefixes |
| routing_policy | enum | latency_preferred | Options: latency_preferred, cost_preferred, region_strict |

Design tradeoffs and notes
- Batching reduces cost but increases tail latency; we provide per-route control and recommended defaults tuned by workload class (chat vs. long-generation).
- Automatic fallback to cheaper quantized variants risks quality regressions; we require model-level regression tests and quality budgets before enabling automatic fallback for a customer.

Roadmap & themes (Q4 2026 -> Q4 2027)
--------------------------------------
Themes by quarter (high level):
- Q4 2026: Core API parity, per-route batching/caching, baseline observability dashboards.
- Q1 2027: Smart routing MVP, canary rollout engine, Reserved capacity beta (Dedicated).
- Q2 2027: Private deployment packaging, KMS/HSM integration, quantization recommendations and profiles.
- Q3 2027: Auto-tuning recommendations (batch/window/quantization) and Redwood Optimize V2 integrations.
- Q4 2027: Enterprise SLAs, multi-region Dedicated, advanced quality monitoring (prompt/eval tie-ins).

Milestones (brief)
1. 2026-12-15: Internal alpha release (API-only) -> limited customers.
2. 2027-03-01: Public beta (Hosted + Console dashboards).
3. 2027-06-15: Dedicated Reserved beta with autoscaling policies.
4. 2027-09-30: Private deployment GA (VPC + on-prem packaging).

Pricing & packaging guidance
---------------------------
Pricing philosophy: Provide clear unit economics for engineering teams with options for low-friction self-serve and enterprise reserved pricing for predictable workloads.
Tiers (examples):
- Hosted Free / Trial: 100k tokens free credits, limited concurrency, no SLA.
- Hosted Standard (pay-as-you-go): per-token generation pricing (e.g. $0.0006 per 1k tokens for base-gen), per-embedding unit price. Includes baseline dashboards and community support.
- Hosted Pro: lower per-token unit cost, higher concurrency, 99.9% availability, email support.
- Dedicated (Reserved): monthly/yearly commitments for GPU pools; pricing modeled as committed vGPU-hours + tail-band burst fees. Typical enterprise commit sizes: $50k/mo+.
- Private: license fee + deployment package + optional support/retainer. Pricing includes deployment service and annual support.

Discounts and add-ons:
- Commit discounts: 20-40% depending on 12-36 month term and committed spend.
- Add-ons: Extended observability retention, compliance package (SOC2/ISO evidence kit), premium SLAs, private-region deployments.

Packaging notes:
- Provide clear migration playbooks (Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private) with performance profiling step and recommended config snapshot for each workload.
- Offer a Dedicated trial for platform evaluation with constrained quotas to showcase autoscaling and routing.

Launch and go-to-market plan (summary)
-------------------------------------
- Developer-first: Quickstarts, SDK examples, and a migration checklist in eng-developer-experience.
- Content & benchmarks: Publish latency/cost benchmarks and reference prompts across tiers.
- Sales-assisted enterprise: Target platform teams with >$50k/mo equivalent run-rate for Dedicated/Private outreach.

Release notes (current release: Unified Inference v1.0 - Public Beta, 2027-03-01)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Highlights:
- Public Beta of Unified Inference: generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking via the unified API.
- Per-route batching and KV-prefix caching enabled for all beta customers.
- Basic Smart Router (latency_preferred policy) with model fallback support in edge cases.
- Redwood Console: per-route dashboards for tokens, cost, latency (p50/p95) and error rates.
- Known issues:
  - Quantized fallback for certain BLOOM-style models may produce higher variance in quality; regression tests and opt-out flags available.
  - Edge-case where batch_window_ms=0 with long-running generators can cause timeouts; default corrected in console UI.

Rollout plan and operational runbook (abridged)
-----------------------------------------------
1. Enable public beta toggle per customer in console.
2. Run performance profile job (automated) for customer sample workloads; capture recommended batch/caching config.
3. Gradual traffic ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over 48 hours, monitor latency p95 and error rate.
4. If error rate > 2% or p95 > threshold for more than 30 mins, execute rollback playbook: revert routing policy to previous model version, notify SRE and account rep.

Appendices
---------
A. Migration checklist (hosted -> dedicated)
  1. Run profiling job and capture perf profile.
  2. Apply recommended batching + caching per route.
  3. Smoke test in Dedicated staging pool.
  4. Schedule cutover with 2-hour maintenance window.

B. Troubleshooting quick tips
  - High tail latency: reduce max_batch_tokens, enforce per-request max latency, or pin to latency_preferred routing.
  - Unexpected cost spike: inspect per-route token breakdown, check cache hit-rate, disable automatic quantized fallback for the route.
